Ha!  They will come whether you let them or not!
column2: 哈！你讓不讓她們來，她們都會來！

column1: No thanks, we Franklins have always rolled our own.
column2: 不用了，我們富蘭克林家一向自己來。

column1: Hmmm^\255\003Seeing as I'm not yet the most powerful man on Earth^\255\003^I may need some help later if I have to launch this thing again.
column2: 嗯^\255\003既然我還不是地表最強之人^\255\003^要是得再放一次，我晚點可能需要幫手。

column1: There will be power enough for all, in time.\255\003There aren't any time machines yet, anyway.
column2: 時候到了，力量會多到人人有份。\255\003反正現在也還沒有時光機。

column1: Using one of my newest inventions.
I like to call it^\255\003THE FRANK-O-COPTER!
column2: 我喜歡叫它^\255\003法蘭克直升機！

column1: That's a kite, Ben.\255\003They've been around for thousands of years.
column2: 那是風箏，班。\255\003這東西存在幾千年了。

column1: Oh, sure^\255\003^as toys.\255\003But this one is a letter to the gods!
column2: 喔，是啊^\255\003^當玩具。\255\003但這一只是寫給諸神的信！

column1: It says, `Dear Thor, just one drop of your mighty juice^\255\003^in the hands of a genius like me^\255\003^could illuminate the entire world!
column2: 上面寫著：`親愛的索爾，只要您那強大電漿的一滴^\255\003^交到我這種天才手上^\255\003^就能照亮整個世界！

column1: I hope you wrote it in Swedish so Thor can read it.
column2: 希望你是用瑞典文寫的，這樣索爾才看得懂。
還是說那些傢伙是挪威人？

column1: I was speaking figuratively.\255\003What actually is happening is that I'm waiting for lightning to strike my kite.
column2: 我那是比喻。\255\003實際上是我在等閃電打中我的風箏。

column1: Aren't you missing a key or something?
column2: 你是不是少了一把鑰匙之類的？

column1: Isn't it too sunny for lightning?
column2: 這麼大太陽哪來的閃電？

column1: Well, I'm going to back away now, just in case.
column2: 那我先退開一點，以防萬一。

column1: The key to discovery is DARING INTELLECT, my boy!\255\003Daring intellect and rigorous science!
column2: 發現的關鍵是「大膽的才智」，孩子！\255\003大膽的才智與嚴謹的科學！

column1: No, I mean a real key-key.
column2: 不，我是說真的那種鑰匙。

column1: You mean, the `Where the heck did I put my keys?` kind of key?
column2: 你是說 `我到底把鑰匙放哪了？` 的那種鑰匙？

column1: That's a manual device!\255\003It needs no power!\255\003Seriously man, what are you thinking?
column2: 那是手動裝置！\255\003根本不用電！\255\003老兄，你到底在想什麼？

column1: Shhh!\255\003I know that.\255\003I'm just trying to keep my grant going until we get a storm.
column2: 噓！\255\003我知道。\255\003我只是想撐著經費，撐到起風暴為止。

column1: And then the electricity charges the kite.
column2: 然後電就會把風箏充飽。

column1: Then the electricity travels down the string.
column2: 然後電會順著線傳下來。

column1: I glow with its almighty power.
column2: 我會因那全能的力量而發光。

column1: I use its power to make the world a better place.
column2: 我要用那份力量讓世界更美好。

column1: The world kneels before me, asking me to guide it with my mighty benevolence.
column2: 全世界跪在我面前，求我以我強大的仁慈引領它。

column1: I have all annoying pests like you locked up.
column2: 我會把你這種煩人的害蟲統統關起來。

column1: You got it^\255\003^just hang on there.
She's too heavy.\255\003I can't control her!

column2: 她要解體了！\255\001她要解體了！

column1: Look at her go!\255\003Now all we need is a little--
column2: 你看她飛的！\255\003現在我們只需要一點——

column1: Off we go, into the wild blue yonder^
column2: 我們出發囉，飛向那湛藍的遠方^

column1: I think we've got it this time^
If you lick it, you'll shock your tongue.
column2: 你舔它的話舌頭會被電到。

column1: No.\255\003It's right where I want it.
Well, I'M all ready to go.\255\003But I guess I have to wait for Bernard and Laverne.
column2: 我這邊是準備好了。\255\003但我看還是得等伯納和拉玟。

column1: That's no good.\255\003It needs some real JUICE!
column2: 這樣不行。\255\003它需要真正的電力！

column1: I don't want to get locked out.
He's not as striking in person as he is on the dollar bill.
column2: 他本人沒有鈔票上那麼有威嚴。

column1: He looks kind of shifty to me.
They're pretty shaken up already.\255\003I'd better leave them be.
column2: 他們已經夠慌了。\255\003我還是別吵他們。

column1: Thank you, this is exactly the sort of thing I need for the time capsule.\255\003I'll bury it tonight, and it won't be seen for hundreds of years.\255\003Future generations are in your debt.
column2: 謝謝你，這正是我時空膠囊需要的東西。\255\003我今晚就把它埋了，幾百年內不會有人看到。\255\003後世子孫都欠你一份情。

column1: If I had a nickel for every time I've seen that face^
column2: 我每看到那張臉一次就收五分錢的話^

column1: This stuff takes the fun outta graffiti.
column2: 這玩意讓塗鴉一點都不好玩了。

column1: I can't.  Vandalism hasn't been invented yet.
column2: 不行。破壞公物還沒被發明出來。

column1: The father of our country is gazing out at me.
Hmm.  This door appears to be locked.
I should plug that into the battery and get the heck out of here!
column2: 我該把那個插上電池，然後趕快閃人！

column1: I should plug that into the battery, once it's charged.
column2: 等電池充飽，我該把那個插上去。

column1: I should plug that into the super-battery^\255\003^once I get one made.
column2: 等我做出超級電池^\255\003^再把那個插上去。

column1: I don't think it'll get much power from that.
column2: 我看那樣供不了多少電。
那不是班尼迪克・阿諾嗎？

column1: I wonder what idiot started the fire?
column2: 不知道是哪個白痴放的火？

column1: I wonder if they've put the fire out yet?
I hope we can get back to work soon.
column2: 希望我們能快點回去工作。

column1: I bet this never happens to Tom Paine.
column2: 我敢說湯姆・潘恩就不會碰到這種事。

column1: Wasn't Ben Franklin talking about starting some sort of `Fire Department`?
column2: 班・富蘭克林之前不是在講要成立什麼 `消防隊` 嗎？

column1: Not now, son, can't you see we're in the middle of a crisis here?
column2: 現在不行，孩子，沒看到我們正在危機當中嗎？

column1: I'm afraid we're a little busy right now.
